## **Why signed contracts stall before they become operational**


A fully signed SaaS agreement can still leave finance billing on the wrong date. Signing records the parties’ agreement, but it does not put the terms into your billing, support, or customer records. If finance uses the signature date while the order form sets a later service start date, the first invoice may go out early.


The handoff can fail when someone circulates a draft instead of the countersigned agreement or misses an amendment that changed a term. Pricing and seat counts may remain in a PDF, while customer success starts onboarding without seeing a promised implementation milestone. Without an owner for the renewal notice date, you may discover the deadline after the notice window closes.


Pre-signature automation helps you prepare, approve, and sign the agreement. Ongoing contract data management keeps its information available and current over time. The post-signature handoff covers the step between them. You verify the executed terms, assign each term an owner and a destination, and confirm that recipients received the information they need to act.


## **The handoff map: which signed terms need an owner and a destination**


Commercial terms need a destination in billing and account records. Finance typically owns the price, billing schedule, and invoice start date in the billing system. RevOps should record contracted seats in the CRM or provisioning record so the account reflects what the customer bought. The person setting up invoices should check the executed agreement for delayed billing language rather than assuming billing begins on the signature date.


Operational terms belong with the people who must deliver them. Customer success should put onboarding milestones and customer dependencies in the onboarding plan, where the account owner can track them. Support should record service commitments, such as response windows, in the tool used to manage requests. Keep any conditions with the commitment. A response window may apply only during specified hours.


Governance terms need an owner who can act on them. RevOps or finance should track renewal dates, notice deadlines, and notice requirements in the renewal record. Negotiated exceptions carry the greatest handoff risk because they depart from the standard agreement and may not fit an existing field or routine. If a customer negotiated a delayed invoice or a different support commitment, assign that clause to the person responsible for carrying it out, record where they will track it, and retain a link to the signed wording. Ask for legal review when the wording leaves the required action unclear.


## **Field-to-system handoff table**


Use the executed agreement as the source for each value in this illustrative handoff map. The destination depends on your company’s tools.


**Contract field** **Example value** **Destination system** **Responsible team**


Pricing $1,200 per month Billing Finance


Billing date First invoice June 1, 2026 Billing Finance


Seats 25 licensed users Account provisioning Customer success


Service commitment Priority support with a four-hour response time Support tooling Support


Onboarding dependency Customer supplies SSO details by June 5 Onboarding tracker Customer success


Renewal notice Notice due 30 days before annual renewal Contract calendar RevOps


Negotiated exception One-time onboarding fee waived Billing Finance


Treat the destinations as examples, not a required stack. If an exception affects more than one system, assign one person to coordinate the updates and confirm that each recipient has acknowledged them.


## **The operating workflow: from executed file to confirmed handoff**


Use a six-stage workflow named Verify, Capture, Assign, Resolve, Update, and Confirm. The handoff starts with the executed agreement and ends when every signed term has a verified source, an owner, a destination, and acknowledgment that the destination reflects the agreed terms.


## **Step-by-step handoff checklist**


- **Verify the executed version.** Check that all required parties signed and that the file includes the final exhibits, order form, and amendments. Compare the signed file with the deal record, then store its contract ID and location in the handoff record. This prevents an earlier draft or incomplete package from driving billing and service work.
- **Capture the terms people must act on.** Record pricing, billing dates, seat counts, service commitments, onboarding dependencies, renewal notice deadlines, and negotiated exceptions as separate fields. For each value, note where it appears in the executed documents. Check the entries against the signed text rather than copying values from a quote, CRM opportunity, or prior contract.
- **Assign one owner and a destination to each field.** Give billing terms to the person responsible for billing, for example, and service commitments to the person who will track delivery. Record the destination system and a named recipient for each field. A field with no owner or destination remains open even if someone extracted it correctly.
- **Resolve missing or conflicting terms before using them.** Flag any term that appears differently across signed documents or leaves a required decision unclear. Ask the appropriate legal or commercial decision-maker to review the executed language, document their decision, and obtain an amendment if the contract needs correction. Automation should surface these issues, not choose which interpretation governs.
- **Update the business systems.** Send each approved value to its assigned destination, such as a billing system, CRM, or support tool. Compare the saved record with the handoff record, including dates and any exception notes. A successful transfer notification does not prove that the receiving system holds the right value.
- **Confirm that each recipient accepted the handoff.** Ask each owner to acknowledge the terms they will administer and record the acknowledgment date. Follow up on rejected or unconfirmed fields instead of marking the contract complete when the systems have merely been updated.


## **Sample handoff record**


A handoff record lets you check each signed term against its destination and the recipient who confirmed it. This hypothetical record shows how you might document one SaaS subscription after verifying the countersigned agreement and attached order form.


**Contract ID:** SA-1042
**Executed date:** February 10, 2026
**Verified source:** Countersigned agreement and attached order form


**Contract field** **Captured term** **Assigned owner** **Destination system** **Acknowledgment**


Price $1,200 per month Finance Billing Confirmed February 11


Billing date First invoice March 1, then monthly Finance Billing Confirmed February 11


Seats 25 Customer success Account record Confirmed February 11


Service commitment 99.9% monthly uptime Customer success Support tooling Confirmed February 12


Onboarding dependency Customer supplies user list before setup Customer success Onboarding tracker Confirmed February 12


Renewal notice 60 days before term end RevOps Renewal calendar Confirmed February 11


Negotiated exception Net 45 payment terms Finance Billing Confirmed February 11


The acknowledgment dates record when each owner checked the captured term in its destination system, not merely when someone sent the handoff.


## **Where structured contract data and integrations fit**


Structured contract data can help you move signed terms into the systems that act on them.[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) connects electronic signatures with internal approvals, structured contract data, and ongoing contract management. Its structured data can flow into systems such as Stripe and Zendesk. Your team still needs to check which terms each receiving system needs and how data reaches it.


During contract review, Common Paper’s Gerri checks Word and PDF documents against company-defined Smart Playbooks and escalates exceptions to an owner. Gerri does not resolve a missing or conflicting signed term on its own. When a term remains unclear, a person should confirm the executed version and seek legal review where judgment is needed.


## **Common handoff mistakes and how to avoid them**


- RevOps may circulate a late draft instead of the executed agreement. Check signatures, countersignatures, and amendments against the stored executed copy before updating business systems.
- A system update does not confirm that the receiving team understood the term. Ask each owner to check the entered value and record their acknowledgment date.
- Standard fields can hide a negotiated exception. Record the exception with its clause reference, assigned owner, and destination so the receiving team can act on it.
- Ambiguous billing or service language should not become a guessed system value. Pause the update and ask legal to interpret the signed terms before the owner acts.
- A renewal notice date without an owner can go untracked. Assign the date to a person and set a reminder in the tool that person uses.


## **FAQs**


**How does the post-signature handoff differ from contract data management?** The handoff moves terms from an executed agreement into the systems and work queues that need them. Contract data management keeps those terms organized and available throughout the contract’s life, including when you need to check a renewal notice or service commitment later.


**Who should own the handoff?** Assign one coordinator, often in RevOps, to track the handoff through confirmation. Finance should verify billing terms, while customer success should verify onboarding and service commitments. Each recipient should acknowledge the fields they own.


**What should you do when a term is missing or ambiguous?** Check the executed agreement and its incorporated documents first. If they do not resolve the question, record the uncertainty and ask the appropriate commercial owner and legal reviewer before changing billing, access, or service obligations.


**When is the handoff complete?** Close the handoff record after each owner confirms that the destination system reflects the signed terms. A successful data transfer alone does not show that the recipient checked the values or accepted the task.


## **Conclusion**


A signed contract becomes operational only when you verify its terms, assign each obligation an owner, update the right business system, and confirm the recipient has accepted the handoff. Contract management software can help you organize that work.[Common Paper](https://commonpaper.com/) is one option for keeping contract data structured, but no tool can decide who owns an ambiguous commitment. Keep the executed agreement as the source of truth, and seek legal review when a negotiated term needs interpretation.
